source_text: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπιγειον, ὡς ἔφην, εὕρημα τοῦτ̓ αὐτοῖς παρεδόθη, οὐδὲ θνητὴν ἐπίνοιαν φυλάσσειν οὕτως ἀξιοῦσιν ἐπιμελῶς, οὐδὲ ἀνθρωπίνων οἰκονομίαν μυστηρίων πεπίστευνται. ἀλλ’ αὐτὸς ἀληθῶς ὁ παντοκράτωρ καὶ παντοκτίστης καὶ ἀόρατος θεός, αὐτὸς ἀπ’ οὐρανῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν καὶ τὸν λόγον τὸν ἅγιον καὶ ἀπερινόητον ἀνθρώποις ἐνίδρυσε καὶ ἐγκατεστήριξε ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν: οὐ, καθάπερ ἄν τις εἰκάσειεν, ἀνθρώποις ὑπηρέτην τινὰ πέμψας ἢ ἄγγελον ἢ ἄρχοντα ἤ τινα τῶν διεπόντων τὰ ἐπίγεια ἤ τινα τῶν πεπιστευμένων τὰς ἐν οὐρανοῖς διοικήσεις, ἀλλ’ αὐτὸν τὸν τεχνίτην καὶ δημιουργὸν τῶν ὅλων, ᾧ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἔκτισεν, ᾧ τὴν θάλασσαν ἰδίοις ἐνέκλεισεν, οὗ τὰ μυστήρια πιστῶς πάντα φυλάσσει τὰ στοιχεῖα, παῤ οὗ τὰ μέτρα τῶν τῆς ἡμέρας δρόμων ὁ ἥλιος εἴληφε φυλάσσειν, ᾧ πειθαρχεῖ σελήνη νυκτὶ φαίνειν κελεύοντι, ᾧ πειθαρχεῖ τὰ ἄστρα: τῷ τῆς σελήνης ἀκολουθοῦντα δρόμῳ: ᾧ πάντα διατέτακται καὶ διώρισται καὶ ὑποτέτακται, οὐρανοὶ καὶ τὰ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, γῆ καὶ τὰ ἐν τῇ γῇ, θάλασσα καὶ τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, πῦρ, ἀήρ, ἄβυσσος, τὰ ἐν ὕψεσι, τὰ ἐν βάθεσι, τὰ ἐν τῷ μεταξύ: τοῦτον πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἀπέστειλεν. ἆρά γε, ὡς ἀνθρώπων ἄν τις λογίσαιτο, ἐπὶ τυραννίδι καὶ φόβῳ καὶ καταπλήξει; οὐ μὲν οὖν: ἀλλ’ ἐν ἐπιεικείᾳ καὶ πραΰτητι ὡς βασιλεὺς πέμπων υἱὸν βασιλέα ἔπεμψεν, ὡς θεὸν ἔπεμψεν, ὡς ἄνθρωπον πρὸς ἀνθρώπους ἔπεμψεν, ὡς σώζων ἔπεμψεν, ὡς πείθων, οὐ βιαζόμενος: βία γὰρ οὐ πρόσεστι τῷ θεῷ. ἔπεμψεν ὡς καλῶν, οὐ διώκων: ἔπεμψεν ὡς ἀγαπῶν, οὐ κρίνων. πέμψει γὰρ αὐτὸν κρίνοντα: καὶ τίς αὐτοῦ τὴν παρουσίαν ὑποστήσεται; ... .. παραβαλλομένους θηρίοις, ἵνα ἀρνήσωνται τὸν κύριον, καὶ μὴ νικωμένους; οὐχ ὁρᾷς, ὅσῳ πλείονες κολάζονται, τοσούτῳ πλεονάζοντας ἄλλους; ταῦτα ἀνθρώπου οὐ δοκεῖ τὰ ἔργα: ταῦτα δύναμίς ἐστι θεοῦ: ταῦτα τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ δείγματα.
pass_a_gloss: For not earthly, as I said, was this discovery given to them, nor do they consider it worthy to carefully guard a mortal thought, nor do they believe it to be a stewardship of human mysteries. But the almighty and all-creating and invisible God himself, from heaven he established and confirmed the truth and the holy and incomprehensible word to men in their hearts: not, as one might suppose, by sending a servant or an angel or a ruler or one of those who preside over earthly things or one of those entrusted with the administrations in heaven, but the craftsman and creator of all things himself, to whom he created the heavens, to whom he enclosed the sea with its own bounds, by whom all the elements are faithfully kept, from whom the sun received the measures of the daily courses to keep, to whom the moon obeys to shine at night when commanded, to whom the stars obey following the course of the moon: to whom all things have been ordered and divided and subjected, the heavens and the things in the heavens, the earth and the things on the earth, the sea and the things in the sea, fire, air, abyss, the things in the heights, the things in the depths, the things in between: this one he sent to them. Would he, as one might reckon of men, have sent him for tyranny and fear and intimidation? Not at all: but in gentleness and mildness, as a king sending a king, he sent his son, as God he sent him, as a man to men he sent him, as one saving he sent him, as one persuading, not forcing: for force is not suitable for God. He sent him as one calling, not pursuing: he sent him as one loving, not judging. For he will send him judging: and who will endure his presence? ... For those thrown to the beasts, that they might deny the Lord, and not be overcome? Do you not see, the more they are punished, the more others abound? These do not seem to be the works of a man: these are the power of God: these are the signs of his presence.

choices.why: verb meaning to set up or establish

pass_b_english: This was no earthly discovery handed down to them, as I said. They do not regard a mortal thought as worth guarding so carefully, nor do they treat it as a stewardship of human mysteries. Instead, the Almighty, all-creating, invisible God himself established the truth and the holy, incomprehensible Word from heaven, confirming it in human hearts. He did not do this by sending a mere servant, an angel, a ruler, one who governs earthly affairs, or one entrusted with heavenly administrations, as anyone might suppose. He sent the very Craftsman and Creator of all things—the One who fashioned the heavens, who shut the sea within its own bounds, by whom the elements are faithfully maintained, from whom the sun received the measures of its daily courses to keep, to whom the moon obeys the command to shine at night, to whom the stars obey as they follow the moon's course. To him all things have been ordered, divided, and subjected: the heavens and all that is in them, the earth and all that is in it, the sea and all that is in it, fire, air, abyss, the things in the heights, the things in the depths, and the things in between. This is the One he sent to them.

Would anyone, judging by human standards, suppose he sent him for tyranny, fear, and intimidation? Not at all. In gentleness and mildness, like a king sending his son, a king, he sent him. As God he sent him; as a man to men he sent him; as a Savior he sent him, persuading, not forcing—for force has no place with God. He sent him calling, not pursuing; he sent him loving, not judging. For he will send him to judge, and who will endure his presence? ... Consider those thrown to the beasts so that they might deny the Lord rather than be overcome. Do you not see that the more they are punished, the more others increase? These are not the works of a man; these are the power of God; these are the signs of his presence.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text of Epistle to Diognetus 7. Pass A and Pass B both preserve the nuances of the Greek, including the complex list of cosmic order and the characterization of God's sending of the Son. Pass B provides a more fluent rendering of the final section without altering the meaning of the Greek.
